mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a paradoxical labor market shock (e.g., underemployment), which reduces effective labor productivity and consumer purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below 2% for four consecutive months signals a reduction in household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on debt and reduces discretionary spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
